clue.text: Give a talk: 'Medical changes'

indicators.note: the quoted word changes, so its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker announces their lecture title, something like 'Medical changes'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' tells you to rearrange the seven letters of MEDICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically, as when delivering an address to an audience.

clue.text: Discarded actors leading a faction

indicators.note: the actors' word comes in front of the rest, leading it

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
a side is a group or party within a dispute

explanation.surface: Actors who have been dropped from a production go on to lead a breakaway group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown away or rejected has been discarded, a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Number in school creating a stink

indicators.note: the number goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: One particular classroom number in a school is producing a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, unpleasant smell is a synonym for a stink.

clue.text: Boring period in which to get sore troubled

indicators.note: the shuffled word is placed in the word for period

parts.note: a period is a stretch of time

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of sore are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dull stretch of time during which one ends up sore and troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' reads like the mood of the sufferer, but it is the anagram signal; the scramble RESO sits in the period word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious and wearisome is boring, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: What's threatening from having got drunk?

definitions.text: What's threatening from having got drunk?

parts.words: What's threatening from having got drunk?
parts.note: the phrase for the next day is also the name for the hangover a heavy night threatens

explanation.surface: A question about what looms after a bout of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is literally the next morning, and idiomatically the hangover felt then.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the miserable hangover that follows a night of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Unsettled pigs relatively well fed will do this?

definitions.meaning: having no fixed home or ties, drifting

definitions.text: pigs relatively well fed will do this?
definitions.meaning: pigs that are well fed will dig about with their snouts less, read as two words

explanation.surface: A whimsical claim that well-fed pigs end up restless.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs root (forage with their snouts) for food; well-fed ones would root less.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking roots or ties to a place means being unsettled and drifting.

clue.text: His ultimately old-fashioned stuff brings derision

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word His

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental, outdated material

explanation.surface: A man's dated material earns mockery in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and mockery are synonyms of derision.

clue.text: Wet duck is caught finally when chaps come round

indicators.note: the men surround the other pieces, coming round them

parts.note: chaps are men
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of caught

explanation.surface: A duck gets caught and soaked as some men gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it wet, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Huff and puff about editor being a dogmatic person?

indicators.note: the breathing word goes about the editor

parts.note: to huff and puff is to breathe heavily, to gasp

explanation.surface: Someone fumes over an editor as an inflexible stickler.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler who insists rigidly on rules or details is a fussy, doctrinaire sort.

clue.text: Small number entertained by English comedian being cheap

indicators.note: the number is held inside the comedian, as a guest is entertained

parts.note: a comic is a comedian
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A modest audience entertained by an English comic who comes cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpensive, offering good value for money, is a sense close to cheap.

clue.text: Element that's faulty in lamp unit

indicators.note: faulty suggests something broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An element in a lamp unit has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: This precious metal, symbol Pt, is a chemical element.

clue.text: One in time of fast with little yen for being ill-disciplined

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the season of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone fasting for a spell gives in to a small craving and is lax.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenity is leniency or mildness, a laxness about discipline; the clue's sense is loose.

clue.text: Thief has grabbed second dog

indicators.note: the thief's word holds the letter, as if grabbing it

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, so a thief is a pincher

explanation.surface: A thief snatches something in a moment and makes off like a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Doberman is one kind of this German breed, a type of dog.

clue.text: One helps get a horse strapped and bones will be broken

definitions.text: One helps get a horse strapped

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strapping up a horse, with a grim warning that bones will be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: This strap of a bridle passes round the horse's nose, part of its tack.

clue.text: Last character in pub always — long time needed for drinks

indicators.note: this picks the final letter of the word pub

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever-ready
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: The last person in the pub is forever waiting a long time for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages is a general word for drinks of any kind.

clue.text: Edward gets upset about historical object being abandoned

indicators.note: the reversed name goes about the old object
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
a relic is an object surviving from the past

explanation.surface: A man called Edward is upset about an antique being thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so Edward's short form becomes DET, with the old object inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict building or ship is one left abandoned and neglected.

clue.text: Score of a modest batsman? Bit less than a score

definitions.meaning: a cricketer making a small total, under twenty runs
a score is twenty, and this number is one short of it

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's score is the runs made; a 'score' also means twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one below twenty fits both a modest innings and a bit under a score.

clue.text: Some contrary names I met in list

indicators.note: contrary means the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
some of the words supply the letters, which lie inside them

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a few awkward names they met appear in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ESIMETI from 'names I met in'; 'contrary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out items one by one is to list them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Substitute one type of material with another

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
lace is another fabric, an open decorative one

explanation.surface: Swapping one fabric for another.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute something is to put another in its place, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Grower finds sources of delight everywhere in harvest

indicators.note: the two initial letters go inside the harvesting word

parts.note: to garner is to gather in, to harvest

indicators.note: sources are the beginnings, so the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A cultivator finds delight all around at harvest time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grows plants and flowers is a cultivator of a plot.

clue.text: Most unusual member of academy needing support

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a rest is a support, as for an arm or a cue

explanation.surface: An unusual academician who needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of rare means least common, the most unusual.

clue.text: Distance travelled at sea creates bond

definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance of about three nautical miles
to join together in alliance, as nations or clubs do

explanation.surface: A long sea voyage brings people closer together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a measure of distance and a verb meaning to ally or unite.

clue.text: Pit with small stones left for removal

indicators.note: the named letter is to be taken away

parts.note: gravel is a mass of small stones

explanation.surface: A pit is being dug with small stones left over to clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial pit dug in the ground is a tomb for the dead.

clue.text: Supporter on the bench following strict code of behaviour?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a form is a long backless bench, as in old schoolrooms
an ally is someone who backs you

explanation.surface: A supporter sitting on the bench sticks rigidly to rules.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a long bench, as in schools or chapels.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting according to etiquette or convention is an adverbial sense of doing things by the book.

clue.text: One participates in matches with divided loyalties

definitions.text: One participates in matches with divided loyalties

parts.words: One participates in matches with divided loyalties
parts.note: matches are marriages, not sporting fixtures; someone in two at once has split allegiance

explanation.surface: A sportsperson torn between two teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like sport; it means marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone married to two spouses at once is in two marriages with divided loyalty.

clue.text: Draw boat by sea's edge

indicators.note: the edge of a word here is its first letter

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Drawing a boat at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a rough drawing is a verb synonym of draw.

clue.text: One may help someone who finds it hard to hear gun

definitions.text: One may help someone who finds it hard to hear
definitions.meaning: a person who says things again for someone hard of hearing
a firearm that fires several shots without reloading

explanation.surface: A device for the hard of hearing is also a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: One who says things again helps the deaf; a multi-shot rifle is also so named.
